solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Play filmed three times, four times possibly

definitions.meaning: a Terence Rattigan play of 1954, filmed in 1958 and remade for television more than once
the three-times table and the four-times table are two distinct multiplication tables

explanation.surface: A note on how often some stage work has been put on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'times' as multiplication: the three-times and four-times tables are two different ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattigan's drama about guests at a seaside hotel carries this title; school multiplication charts are the other sense.

clue.text: Surrounding temperature troubled Byron's rare war horse

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around another piece, holding it within them
something troubled is stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet's unusual warhorse is upset by the heat around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges BYRONSRAREWAR, and 'Surrounding' puts T inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a horse with a reddish coat flecked with white, famous from the cowboy song.

clue.text: Acclaim mounting for two in the end

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means the letters climb from bottom to top, read backwards
one word placed in the other, held within it

parts.note: a tip is the end of something, such as a pencil
dual means twofold, consisting of two

explanation.surface: Praise rising for a pair of finalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns the whole thing upward, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean public praise or approval, an expression of enthusiastic applause.

clue.text: Tree line primarily advancing north

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of advancing is used

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A line of trees pushing forward toward the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with its red berries, is a common British tree also called by this name.

clue.text: One's liable to hit extremely tough bit of bacon

indicators.note: extremely is read as at the extremes, taking only the two outermost letters of tough

parts.note: a rasher is a thin slice of bacon

explanation.surface: A warning that someone may lash out over a tough piece of breakfast meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who beats or flogs others is one likely to hit; the word also names a bird.

clue.text: Charged like king in Mr Heath's clutches?

indicators.note: the inner pieces are placed in the grip of the outer one
clutches means a grasp, so one piece is held tight inside another

parts.note: Ted Heath was British Conservative prime minister 1970-74
as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A question whether a monarch was accused while in the hands of a former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was UK prime minister in the early 1970s; his first name holds AS and K.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charged with a duty is to be assigned a job to carry out.

clue.text: Those attending during Giselle, eg, shortly to get trifle

indicators.note: during says one piece comes in the middle of another
shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Giselle is a well-known romantic ballet
the gate is the number of people attending an event, as at a football match

explanation.surface: A trifling show for the audience at a performance of Giselle.
explanation.walkthrough: The gate is the crowd that turns up to an event, and Giselle is a classic ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is something of little importance, a mere nothing, as is this word for a small light thing.

clue.text: Parasitic threat to crops having me lower supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: A pest that attacks plants makes me cut the stock I provide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the verb but the adverb 'supplely', bending MELOWER into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A nematode that infests plant roots and stems, this tiny worm damages crops.

clue.text: Visiting gents dispatching a cage nearly empty, to carry piano

indicators.note: one piece carries another, holding it within its letters

parts.note: to dispatch something is to send it
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a pen is an enclosure or cage for animals

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, keeping only the first and last letters of nearly

explanation.surface: Sending off a cage that is almost empty, with a piano carried along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents' is a British name for a men's public lavatory; the idiom comes from the old penny charged to use one.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy British idiom for going to the toilet, from the old penny charged for public lavatories.

clue.text: Men rejected notice — factory disruption on the way

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
an ad is a notice in a newspaper
works is another word for a factory

explanation.surface: Workers turned down a notice and caused trouble at the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' is the crossword convention for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair work on a road holds up traffic, disrupting those travelling along it.

clue.text: Couple dance: miss work

parts.note: a miss is a girl, a gal
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A pair skip a dance and miss work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple dance' is a lively dance for couples, not 'couple' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 19th-century ballroom dance in two-four time, danced by pairs.

clue.text: Expand study by women's organisation

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation
a den is a small private study

explanation.surface: A women's group expands its study.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute (WI) is a large British association of community women's groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand something is to make it broader or more extensive.

clue.text: Veg Tiny Tim initially held in contempt

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another

parts.note: scorn means contempt or disdain
wee is Scottish for small or tiny

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of Tim

explanation.surface: Dickens's Tiny Tim being scorned over his vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny Tim' looks like the Dickens character, but the words split: Tiny gives WEE and 'initially' takes T from Tim.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize kernels eaten as a vegetable, a sweet variety of corn.

clue.text: Authorised denomination housed in terminal

indicators.note: one piece lives inside another

parts.note: the end is the terminal point
a title is a name or denomination

explanation.surface: A sect given authority within an airport building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denomination' suggests a church or banknote, but here it means a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone authorised to do something has a right to it, being permitted.

clue.text: Make sure striker is fit for international?

parts.note: to test is to check, making sure
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A check whether a forward is fit to play for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer, but in the first reading it is a match that gets struck. A test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a game between national teams, chiefly in cricket or rugby, so an example of an international.

clue.text: Student population once almost entirely male in college

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means wholly or entirely

indicators.note: one piece placed in the middle of another

parts.note: uni is a short word for university, a college

explanation.surface: A college whose students were once nearly all men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' belongs to the definition: these are former students.
explanation.definitionFit: Former students of a school or college are its graduates, those who once studied there.

clue.text: Wartime pin-up girl's drawn in poster that can be ordered

indicators.note: the pin-up draws the poster into her name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Betty Grable was the most famous pin-up of the Second World War
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster

explanation.surface: A famous wartime pin-up girl drawn on a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: Betty Grable was the best-known American pin-up of the Second World War; 'drawn in' reads as her name taking in the poster, not her picture on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be put in order or ranked by degree is capable of being graded.

clue.text: Three couples in precipitate entrance

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a precipitate act is hasty or rash
three pairs make six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Three pairs rush in through a hasty doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), to enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to enrapture or delight greatly, as does this verb.

clue.text: Strangling first person, criminal craves guts

indicators.note: the outer piece strangles the inner, gripping it all around
something criminal is crooked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A criminal choking someone has a craving for innards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges CRAVES, and 'Strangling' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The internal organs of the body are its innards, the guts.

clue.text: High jumper got back across free-flowing river

indicators.note: one piece is laid across the other, spanning it
back means the letters are read in reverse
flowing means moving freely, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An athlete returning over a fast-moving river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges FREE into REEF; 'High jumper' looks like an athlete but is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphibian that climbs trees and leaps between branches is a jumper living high up.

clue.text: Left at end of theatre season in Paris more than satisfied

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the end of another

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: Someone who left after a theatre season in Paris and was well pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left at end of theatre' puts L after REP; été is French for summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be full to bursting, having eaten plenty, goes beyond merely being satisfied.

clue.text: Red or white container such as tall staff may have?

definitions.meaning: a large vessel for serving wine

definitions.text: such as tall staff may have?

explanation.surface: A wine jug, or what a high pole might carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as FLAG ON, what a flagstaff has.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug with a handle and spout, often used to serve wine.

clue.text: Favoured second crest, reduced, with coloured frame

indicators.note: the outer piece frames the inner ones, enclosing them

parts.note: red is a colour, so something coloured can be red

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an emblem is a badge or crest

explanation.surface: A popular coat of arms, scaled down and given a coloured border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured' is not 'popular' but 'took after', as a child favours a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour a parent is to look like them, as in 'she favours her mother'.

clue.text: Supplement in honour of youngster

parts.note: a toast is raised to someone, in their honour
a pup is a young animal or cheeky youngster

explanation.surface: An extra allowance paid in a child's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition that brings something back up to full, such as more credit or drink.

clue.text: Tribespeople's trust, oddly, is rising

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth
in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A tribe's faith seems to be growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes TUT from trust, and 'rising' turns IS upward to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a tribal group.

clue.text: Quick drink recruit drained

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, a drink

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its contents, keeping only the outer letters of recruit

explanation.surface: A quick pint for a new soldier who is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-witted and on the ball means being sharp and watchful.

clue.text: Runner's been and got lost, accepting contrary directions

indicators.note: the outer piece accepts, taking in another one
lost means astray, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: W and E, west and east, are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: An athlete who has turned up and then lost the way, going both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges BEENGOT, and 'accepting' takes WE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary who carries messages between two parties, a messenger or runner.

clue.text: One settlement scheme remains to be covered in Tory speech

indicators.note: one piece is covered by another, sitting inside it

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
ash is what remains after burning
delivery is a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A Conservative speech covering ways to settle debts.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is short for Conservative, the party also called Tory; delivery is a speaker's way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of paying for goods when they are handed over is a settlement arrangement.
